You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

import os,subprocess,json,re,pathlib,shutil
EXE='/workspace/executable'
def git(repo,*args,env=None):
 p=subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(repo),*args],capture_output=True,text=True,env=env); assert p.returncode==0,(args,p.stderr);return p.stdout.strip()
def run(repo,*args):
 p=subprocess.run([EXE,str(repo),'-o','json',*args],capture_output=True,text=True)
 if p.returncode:return {'ERROR':p.stderr,'status':p.returncode}
 d=json.loads(p.stdout);return {'title':d['title'],**{k:v for x in d['infoFields'] for k,v in x.items()}}
def commit(repo,name='Alice',email='alice@example.test',date='2023-01-01T12:00:00Z'):
 git(repo,'add','-A');git(repo,'commit','-qm','change','--allow-empty',env={**os.environ,'GIT_AUTHOR_NAME':name,'GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL':email,'GIT_AUTHOR_DATE':date,'GIT_COMMITTER_DATE':date})
def newrepo(name):
 p=pathlib.Path('/tmp/ofprobe')/name;shutil.rmtree(p,ignore_errors=True);p.mkdir();git(p,'init','-q');git(p,'config','user.name','Test User');git(p,'config','user.email','test@example.test');return p
def show(label,d,fields):print(label,{k:d[k] for k in fields.split() if k in d})
if __name__=='__main__':
 p=newrepo('files');(p/'main.py').write_text('x = 1\n');commit(p)
 f='PendingInfo LanguagesInfo LocInfo SizeInfo ChurnInfo LicenseInfo'
 show('clean',run(p),f)
 (p/'main.py').write_text('x = 1\ny = 2\nz = 3\n');(p/'new.js').write_text('const a = 1;\nconst b = 2;\n');(p/'.hidden.py').write_text('x = 9\n');(p/'.secret').mkdir();(p/'.secret'/'hide.rs').write_text('fn main() {}\n');(p/'unknown.bin').write_bytes(b'\0'*10000)
 show('dirty',run(p),f);show('hidden',run(p,'--include-hidden'),f)
 (p/'.gitignore').write_text('new.js\nunknown.bin\n');show('ignored',run(p,'--include-hidden'),f)
 git(p,'add','main.py');(p/'main.py').unlink();show('staged,deleted',run(p),f)
 (p/'main.py').write_text('x=1\n');commit(p)
 show('committed',run(p),f);show('ex *.py',run(p,'-e','*.py'),f);show('ex all',run(p,'-e','*'),f)
 (p/'LICENSE').write_text('MIT\n');(p/'package.json').write_text('{"license":"Apache-2.0"}');show('license short',run(p),f)
 (p/'LICENSE').unlink();show('license package',run(p),f)
 (p/'sub').mkdir();(p/'sub'/'hello.go').write_text('package main\nfunc main() {}\n');show('subdir path',run(p/'sub'),f+' ProjectInfo')
PY

import subprocess,re,json,pathlib
E='/workspace/executable';R='/tmp/ofprobe/alpha'
def run(*args):
 p=subprocess.run([E,*args],capture_output=True,text=True)
 if p.returncode:raise RuntimeError((args,p.stderr))
 return p.stdout
fields='project description head pending version created languages dependencies authors last-change contributors url commits churn lines-of-code size license'.split()
list_text=run('-l')
p=subprocess.run([E,'-a','invalid'],capture_output=True,text=True)
keys=re.search(r'\[possible values: (.*)\]',p.stderr)[1].split(', ')
data={'help_long':run('--help'),'help_short':run('-h'),'languages':list_text,'keys':keys,'logos':{},'completions':{}}
# Identify color positions using distinct, CLI-selected ANSI colors.
for key in keys:
 base=[R,'--no-title','--no-color-palette','-d',*fields,'-a',key]
 normal=run(*base,'--true-color','never')
 rgb=run(*base,'--true-color','always')
 indexed=run(*base,'-c','0','1','2','3','4','5')
 def unframe(x):return x.removeprefix('\x1b[?7l').removesuffix('\x1b[?7h')
 normal,rgb,indexed=map(unframe,(normal,rgb,indexed))
 pattern=r'\x1b\[([0-9;]+)m'
 a=re.findall(pattern,normal);b=re.findall(pattern,rgb);c=re.findall(pattern,indexed)
 palette={};true_palette={}
 assert len(a)==len(b)==len(c),key
 for x,y,z in zip(a,b,c):
  z=z.removesuffix(';1')
  if z in ('30','31','32','33','34','35'):
   idx=str(int(z)-30);palette[idx]=x.removesuffix(';1');true_palette[idx]=y.removesuffix(';1')
 def replace(m):
  color=m[1].removesuffix(';1')
  if color=='0':return ''
  if color=='39':return ''
  return '{'+str(int(color)-30)+'}'
 # The UI adds right padding after the final colored piece. It is saved separately.
 lines=[]
 for line in indexed.splitlines():
  matches=list(re.finditer(pattern,line));end=matches[-1].end() if matches else 0
  pad=line[end:]
  lines.append([re.sub(pattern,replace,line[:end]),len(pad)])
 # The title color can differ from the first logo color for some logos.
 title=run(R,'--no-art','--no-color-palette','-d',*fields,'-a',key,'--true-color','never')
 title_rgb=run(R,'--no-art','--no-color-palette','-d',*fields,'-a',key,'--true-color','always')
 title_color=re.search(pattern,title)[1].removesuffix(';1')
 title_rgb_color=re.search(pattern,title_rgb)[1].removesuffix(';1')
 data['logos'][key]={'lines':lines,'colors':palette,'rgb_colors':true_palette,'title':title_color,'title_rgb':title_rgb_color}
for shell in ['bash','elvish','fish','powershell','zsh']:
 data['completions'][shell]=run('--generate',shell)
# Data is an application resource: text displayed by its user interface.
p=pathlib.Path('/workspace/onefetch_impl/ui.py')
p.write_text('"""Terminal artwork and fixed interface text, recorded from CLI observations."""\n\nUI = '+repr(data)+'\n')
print('Stored',len(keys),'logos; UI resource',p.stat().st_size,'bytes')
PY

"""Regression checks for observed CLI behavior, with isolated local Git fixtures."""
import json
import os
import pathlib
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PROGRAM=ROOT/'executable'

class RepositoryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp=tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.repo=pathlib.Path(self.temp.name)/'project'
        self.repo.mkdir()
        self.env={**os.environ,'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL':'/dev/null','GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM':'1',
                  'GIT_AUTHOR_DATE':'2020-01-02T03:04:05+02:00',
                  'GIT_COMMITTER_DATE':'2020-01-02T03:04:05+02:00'}
        self.git('init','-q','-b','main')
        self.git('config','user.name','Test Author')
        self.git('config','user.email','author@example.test')
        self.source='# heading\n\nx = 1\nprint(x)\n'
        (self.repo/'app.py').write_text(self.source)
        self.manifest=json.dumps({'name':'demo','version':'0.9.0','description':'Small demonstration',
                                  'license':'MIT','dependencies':{'a':'1','b':'2'},
                                  'devDependencies':{'c':'3'}})
        (self.repo/'package.json').write_text(self.manifest)
        self.git('add','.')
        self.git('commit','-qm','Initial commit')
        self.git('tag','v1.2.3')
        self.git('branch','feature')
        self.git('remote','add','origin','https://user:token@example.test/org/demo.git')
    def tearDown(self):self.temp.cleanup()
    def git(self,*args):
        p=subprocess.run(['git','-C',str(self.repo),*args],env=self.env,check=True,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        return p.stdout.decode().strip()
    def invoke(self,*args):
        return subprocess.run([str(PROGRAM),str(self.repo),*args],env=self.env,capture_output=True,text=True)
    def info(self,*args):
        result=self.invoke('-o','json','-z',*args)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        data=json.loads(result.stdout)
        fields={k:v for item in data['infoFields'] for k,v in item.items()}
        return data,fields
    def test_metadata(self):
        data,f=self.info('--no-title')
        self.assertIsNone(data['title'])
        self.assertEqual(f['ProjectInfo'],{'repoName':'demo','numberOfBranches':0,'numberOfTags':1})
        self.assertEqual(f['VersionInfo']['version'],'v1.2.3')
        self.assertEqual(f['CreatedInfo']['creationDate'],'2020-01-02T01:04:05Z')
        self.assertEqual(f['HeadInfo']['headRefs']['refs'],['main'])
        self.assertEqual(f['HeadInfo']['headRefs']['shortCommitId'],self.git('rev-parse','HEAD')[:7])
        self.assertEqual(f['DependenciesInfo']['dependencies'],'2 (Npm)')
        self.assertEqual(f['LicenseInfo']['license'],'MIT')
        self.assertEqual(f['LanguagesInfo']['languagesWithPercentage'],[{'language':'Python','percentage':100.0}])
        self.assertEqual(f['LocInfo']['linesOfCode'],2)
        self.assertEqual(f['SizeInfo']['fileCount'],2)
        self.assertEqual(f['SizeInfo']['repoSize'],str(len(self.source)+len(self.manifest))+' B')
        self.assertEqual(f['UrlInfo']['repoUrl'],'https://user:redacted@example.test/org/demo.git')
        self.assertEqual(f['CommitsInfo'],{'numberOfCommits':1,'isShallow':False})
    def test_flags_and_visibility(self):
        data,f=self.info('--email','--hide-token','--number-of-languages','0','-d','head','churn')
        self.assertNotIn('HeadInfo',f)
        self.assertNotIn('ChurnInfo',f)
        self.assertEqual(f['AuthorsInfo']['authors'][0]['email'],'author@example.test')
        self.assertEqual(f['UrlInfo']['repoUrl'],'https://example.test/org/demo.git')
        self.assertIn('LanguagesInfo',f) # the language limit only affects the legend
        p=self.invoke('--no-art','--no-color-palette','--no-title','--no-bold','-d','churn')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.startswith('\x1b[?7l'))
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.endswith('\x1b[?7h'))
        self.assertNotIn(';1m',p.stdout)
        self.assertNotIn('git version',p.stdout)
    def test_worktree_versus_index(self):
        (self.repo/'app.py').write_text(self.source+'x += 1\n')
        (self.repo/'extra.js').write_text('const y = 3;\n')
        _,f=self.info()
        self.assertEqual(f['PendingInfo'],{'added':1,'deleted':0,'modified':1})
        self.assertEqual(f['LocInfo']['linesOfCode'],4)
        self.assertEqual(f['SizeInfo']['fileCount'],2)
        self.git('add','app.py','extra.js')
        _,f=self.info()
        self.assertEqual(f['PendingInfo'],{'added':0,'deleted':0,'modified':0})
        self.assertEqual(f['SizeInfo']['fileCount'],3)
    def test_hidden_and_excluded(self):
        (self.repo/'.hidden').mkdir()
        (self.repo/'.hidden'/'code.rs').write_text('fn main() {}\n'*4)
        _,normal=self.info()
        _,hidden=self.info('--include-hidden')
        _,excluded=self.info('--include-hidden','-e','*.{py,rs}')
        self.assertEqual(normal['LocInfo']['linesOfCode'],2)
        self.assertEqual(hidden['LocInfo']['linesOfCode'],6)
        self.assertNotIn('LocInfo',excluded)
    def test_empty_commit_tree_and_errors(self):
        bad=self.invoke('--output','bad-format')
        self.assertEqual(bad.returncode,2)
        self.assertIn('[possible values: json, yaml]',bad.stderr)
        missing=subprocess.run([str(PROGRAM),str(self.repo/'does-not-exist')],capture_output=True,text=True)
        self.assertEqual(missing.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn('path is not a directory',missing.stderr)
        image=self.invoke('--image','missing.png')
        self.assertEqual(image.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn('No such file or directory (os error 2)',image.stderr)
    def test_yaml_and_crlf_sizes(self):
        p=self.invoke('-o','yaml','--no-title','-d','churn')
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode,0)
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.startswith('title: null\ninfoFields:\n- ProjectInfo:\n'))
        self.git('config','core.autocrlf','true')
        (self.repo/'crlf.py').write_bytes(b'x=1\r\ny=2\r\n')
        self.git('add','crlf.py')
        _,f=self.info()
        self.assertEqual(f['SizeInfo']['repoSize'],str(len(self.source)+len(self.manifest)+10)+' B')

class FixedInterfaceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_version_and_lists(self):
        def run(*args):return subprocess.check_output([str(PROGRAM),*args],text=True)
        self.assertEqual(run('--version'),'onefetch 2.25.0\n')
        self.assertEqual(run('--package-managers'),'Npm\nCargo\n')
        self.assertEqual(len(run('--languages').splitlines()),117)
        self.assertIn('Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [INPUT]',run('--help'))
        self.assertTrue(run('--generate','fish').startswith('complete -c onefetch'))

if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()

Python zip application. It uses Python 3's standard library and the installed
Git CLI; no downloadable packages or project-specific dependencies are required.
The executable works independently of the source directory.

interface, not as a substitute for the information display or language counter.

    def test_empty_commit_tree_and_errors(self):
